p: vain knowledge: That is, vain words, and without consolation?
with the east wind: Meaning, with matters that are of no importance, which are forgotten as soon as they are uttered, as the East wind dries up moisture as soon as it falls.
fear: He charges Job as though his talk caused men to cast off the fear of God and prayer.
tongue of the crafty: You speak as the mockers and contemners of God do.
first man that was born: That is, the most ancient and so by reason the most wise?
to thyself: Are you only wise?
small with thee: He accuses Job's pride and ingratitude, that will not be comforted by God, but by their counsel.
carry thee away: Why do you stand in your own conceit?
be righteous: His purpose is to prove that Job, as an unjust man and a hypocrite, is punished for his sins, as he did before, Job 4:8.
drinketh iniquity like water: Who has a desire to sin, as he who is thirsty to drink.
given: Who by their wisdom so governed, that no stranger invaded them, and so the land seemed to be given to them alone.
of years is hidden to the: The cruel man is always in danger of death, and is never quiet in conscience.
darkness: Out of that misery to which he once fell.
abroad for bread: God not only impoverishes the wicked often, but even in their prosperity he punishes them with a greediness to gain even more: which is as a beggary.
anguish shall make him afraid: He shows the weapons God uses against the wicked, who lift up themselves against him, that is, terror of conscience and outward afflictions.
his fatness: That is, he was so puffed up with prosperity and abundance for all things, that he forgave God: noting that Job in his happiness did not have the true fear of God.
in desolate cities: Though he build and repair ruinous places to gain fame, yet God will bring all to nothing, and turn his great prosperity into extreme misery.
perfection thereof upon the earth: Meaning, that his sumptuous buildings would never come to perfection.
deceived trust in vanity: He stands in his own conceit, that he will give no place to good counsel, therefore his own pride will bring him to destruction.
grape as the vine: As one who gathers grapes before they are ripe.
bribery: Who were built or maintained by bribery.
conceive mischief: Therefore all their vain devises will turn to their own destruction.
